newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen stocks skid to lower end on policy talk.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen stocks skid to lower end on policy talk.

text.p: Shenzhen's stock indices on Tuesday slid to a sharply lower close as talk of new government policies to cool down trading swirled through the markets, brokers said.
The foreign currency B index plunged 5.13 points or 2.80 percent to 178.37 on turnover of HK$137.8 million compared with Monday's HK$184.3 million.
The domestic currency A share index ended 14.50 points or 2.65 percent lower at 531.52 on turnover of 16.3 billion yuan against Monday's 20.8 billion.
"Today's sharp falls were driven by expectations of policy changes," an analyst at Chnna Southern Securities said.
Traders said the rumours referred to the possibilty of the government allowing some previously non-tradable institutional shares to enter the secondary market.
"This could hugely inflate the market size and the existing funds may not be able to provide sufficient support," the China Southern analyst said.
The indices are seen as having the potential to move sharply in either direction in the short term given the market's volatile mood, analysts said.
"It's very hard to make a bet now," an analyst at J&A Securities said. "People are poking their ears up to try to sense what the government may do."
Securities authorities were also said to extend the transaction settlement period to three days to reduce market volatility, traders said.
This compares with the current settlement period of one day for A shares and immediate settlement for B shares.
"This could dry up market liquidity," the J&A analyst said.
A Hong Kong newspaper on Tuesday said Chinese authorities had decided they would no longer tolerate the recent "crazy" market gains, and would announce clampdown measures in the short term.
"Apart from extending the settlement period, the government is also seen likely to rein in several brokerages," an analyst at a major investment bank said.
Chiwan Wharf Holdings Ltd was the worst performer in the B share market, losing HK$0.38 or 6.69 percent to HK$5.30.
In the A share market, Shenzhen Textile Holdings Co Ltd was one of the sharpest losers, shedding 1.00 yuan or 7.13 percent to 13.03 yuan.
